title: The vehicles you can use
summary: Supermarket Simulator has vehicles of its own rather than only trolleys: the game sells them as items, lets a player get in and out, and moves stock from them.
body: Vehicles are items in the shop. The game has a sale item for a vehicle, which is why one can be bought as its own purchase rather than arriving with an order.
There is more than one kind. The game keeps a bike configuration and its own wheel and controller, so what you drive is a defined kind of vehicle rather than one generic model.
A player gets in and out. The game has an interaction for a vehicle and a place for a driver to sit, which is why driving is a state you enter rather than a vehicle that moves by itself.
Stock moves from one. The game keeps vehicle boxes and a restock area controller, so stock can be dealt with at a vehicle rather than only at a shelf.
They are carried on the network. Vehicles have their own networked behaviour and even a separate mode, which is why a shared shop sees the same vehicle being used.
They come with settings. The game keeps vehicle data and a loader for it, so a vehicle is configured by the game rather than hard-wired into a level.
What this entry does not tell you: what a vehicle costs, how fast one goes, or how much it carries. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Vehicles are sold as items in the shop.
One of the vehicles is a bike with its own configuration, wheels and controller.
A player enters and leaves a vehicle, and has a driver state.
Stock is handled at a vehicle, with its own boxes and restock area.
Vehicles have networked behaviour of their own.
A driver has targets of their own for sitting in the vehicle.
